newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Monday's loss and analysts said the market would likely fall again on Wednesday, maintaining its three-month flat trend after having risen during the last three sessions last week.
Analysts said large primary market offers, the listing of National Investment Funds (NFIs) and elections due in September were restricting buying despite Poland's strong economy.

"There seems to be no new money entering the market; some money flowed to the Funds though it's hard to say to what degree it was speculative and to what degree new capital," said Cezary Pospieszynski of Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.9 percent to 16,103.3 points and turnover fell 10 percent to 112.8 million zlotys ($34.8 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 56 to 28 with 21 stocks stable.
The funds' NIF index dropped 5.5 percent on Tuesday to 160.1 points after having eased on Monday and surging 6.4 percent on Friday, the day after their debut.
Analysts said both the NIF index and NFI units, down 3.4 percent on Tuesday to 154.5 zlotys ($47.6), could fall again on Wednesday and that their price convergence could continue.
They said some stocks could be affected by May earnings reports due on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Some analysts said if Bank Handlowy's final issue price, due on Tuesday, came in toward the top of its 28-35 zloty ($8.6-10.8) price range, the market could get a temporary psychological lift.
Analysts said good economic news included Monday's news of 0.6-percent year-on-year inflation in May and Poland's Tuesday cut of its 1997 y-o-y inflation target to 12 from 13 percent.
They were surprised by biggest loser bank WBK's 9.9 percent drop in moderate trade.
